one_liner: Intercom has a REST API with OAuth 2.0 for public apps and static Access Tokens for private apps, plus a free US-only developer workspace. Publishing a multi-customer app needs Intercom review. The MCP claim could not be verified from the supplied pages.
auth_notes: The docs page confirms OAuth for public apps that access other people's data, and an Access Token for private apps on your own workspace. The claims that OAuth tokens never expire and that there are no refresh tokens are not on the supplied pages.
access_notes: A free development workspace gives access to the Developer Hub, where you can configure webhooks and set up OAuth. It is US-region only and has limited functionality compared with a paid workspace. The supplied pages do not settle whether production API use needs a paid plan. The draft's FAQ quote about upgrading is not on any supplied page. Intercom itself offers a 14-day free trial.
blocker_notes: Private-app tokens need no review. A public OAuth app that other customers can install has to be submitted to Intercom for review. The dev workspace is US-only and limited, and production workspaces may need a paid plan, which the pages do not settle.

evidence.quote: Private apps are apps that you can build specifically for your Intercom workspace that only access your own data. You can build a private app using your Access Token and it does not require a review.
